title: Self-consistent band structure calculation
action: For each material (Si, Ge, α-Sn), set up the diamond-structure unit cell with the given lattice constant and atomic positions. Construct the starting screened pseudopotential using the ionic pseudopotential parameters and the Heine-Abarenkov dielectric function. Perform a self-consistent field (SCF) loop: solve the Schrödinger equation in a plane-wave basis, using Baldereschi's special k-point for the charge density and a finer k-point mesh for band energies. Use the Xα exchange-correlation with α=0.79. Iterate until eigenvalues are stable. After convergence, extract the band eigenvalues at the Γ, X, and L high-symmetry points.
description: Self-consistent field calculation to obtain wavefunctions, charge density, and screened potential for each material.

title: Total energy computation
action: Using the self-consistent wavefunction coefficients, charge density Fourier components, and screening potentials from the SCF step, compute the total crystal energy per atom via the momentum-space total-energy formula of Ihm, Zunger, and Cohen. Include the sum of occupied eigenvalues, the Hartree and exchange-correlation double-counting corrections, the core repulsiveness term α₁Z, and the Ewald ion-ion energy.
description: Post-process the SCF results to compute the total energy per atom.

title: Output band energies and total energy
action: Assemble the computed band eigenvalues and total energies into the specified JSON structure. For each material, provide the energy eigenvalues at the Γ, X, and L points in eV, referenced to the top of the valence band (Γ₂₅' set to 0 eV), and the total crystal energy per atom in Ryd. Write the result to band_and_total_energy.json under /app/outputs.
description: A JSON object with key 'materials' containing a list of material entries. Each entry has 'name' (one of 'Si', 'Ge', 'alpha-Sn'), 'band_eigenvalues' (an object with keys 'Gamma', 'X', 'L'), and 'total_energy_per_atom' (float in Ryd). The eigenvalue lists must follow this order: Gamma: [Γ₁ (lowest valence), Γ₂₅' (top of valence, must be ~0), Γ₁₅, Γ₂', Γ₁₂' (if available)]; X: [X₁ (lowest valence), X₄, X₁ (conduction), X₄ (upper conduction)]; L: [L₂' (lowest valence), L₁, L₃', L₁ (conduction), L₃]. All energies relative to Γ₂₅'.
